name: Red Wool Bandana
summary: Inside the Stormwind Stockade, Red Wool Bandana scraps mark Defias brotherhood. Imprisoned cutthroats tear them from jailhouse wool blankets and wear them as emblems of defiance behind bars.

sections.title: Stitched in Defiance
sections.body: In the Stormwind Stockade, Defias Brotherhood inmates hold fast to their identity. They secretly tear scraps from prison wool blankets and stitch them into red bandanas to wear as their colors. Guards treat the scarves as contraband, and their discovery can spark fatal mutinies. For the prisoners, each bandana declares that their brotherhood and rebellion endure, even in chains.

sections.title: A Grandmother's Vengeance
sections.body: Red Wool Bandanas became known for the death of Mac Raskol, a fourteen-year-old prison guard. He caught inmates shredding blankets to make the scarves and tried to discipline them. Defias convicts stabbed him in the back. His grieving grandmother, Nikova, now seeks adventurers to enter the rioting dungeon, cull the rioters, and bring back the crimson cloth as proof of vengeance.

faq.q: Where do prisoners get these bandanas in the Stockade?
aliases: how do they make red bandanas
faq.answer: Defias inmates tear the bandanas from their prison-issue wool blankets. Disarmed and imprisoned, they turn their meager bedding into signs of defiance to wear inside the cells.

Nikova Raskol, a grieving grandmother in Stormwind, asks adventurers to collect the bandanas. Her fourteen-year-old grandson Mac guarded the Stockade and was murdered by prisoners after he caught them making the scarves.

faq.q: Why do the prisoners care so much about wearing red scarves?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood uses red masks and bandanas as its gang colors and uniform. Behind bars, the scraps let inmates keep their rank, morale, and unity.
Almost any rioting Defias member in the Stockade carries one, including Defias Captives, Inmates, Prisoners, Insurgents, and Convicts.

angles.text: For Alliance defenders, recovering these bandanas brings grim justice for young Mac Raskol and strikes at the rioters holding the city's prison.
These rough bandanas show how desperate hands in captivity can unravel coarse wool blankets and put the fibers to use again.
